title: Boston Dynamics gives more insight into its redesigned humanoid hand
key_facts: Boston Dynamics showed a new four-fingered hand for its Atlas humanoid robot last week; it has 13 degrees of freedom and is directly actuated.
The company dropped the pinky finger and reduced the size of the gripper; it says the hand is designed for mass manufacturing and still handles over 100 lb.
Alberto Rodriguez, director of robot behavior for Atlas, says the hand is built from 13 identical, fully encapsulated actuators with no fragile cables crossing joints.
The hand was designed so it can be simulated accurately, to allow reinforcement learning (trial-and-error training) in simulation to carry over to the real hand.
Rodriguez said a two-thumb design was rejected because it added actuation complexity, extra degrees of freedom, cost and volume.
Test tasks include handheld power tools, handling cables and fishing for screws; the team has also tried juggling and speed hand games.
Rodriguez said the hands have been used extensively at headquarters but not yet deployed across the whole robot fleet.
